newsitem.title: USA: Toyota's Lexus plans sport utility vehicle.
newsitem.headline: Toyota's Lexus plans sport utility vehicle.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp's Lexus Division said on Thursday it will introduce a new car-based utility vehicle in the first half of 1998.

James Press, general manager of the Lexus Divison, told reporters at the Chicago Auto Show that the new vehicle, which will be similar to a concept model introduced here, will compete in the "near luxury" end of the sport utility market with vehicles now priced at about $30,000 to $35,000.
Press said the new vehicle will have an estimated annual sales volume of about 22,000 to 42,000 units, which would make it Lexus's second-best selling vehicle behind the ES300 luxury sedan.

The new vehicle, which appeared as the Sport Luxury Vehicle (SLV), is based on the ES300 car platform and is designed to minimize negative attributes normally found in truck-based sport utility vehicles and will offer a more comfortable ride and better fuel economy.
The vehicle will be built at Toyota's Kyushu, Japan, factory.
